import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianMixtureCoupling
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinLipschitzLower
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space

/-!
# Quadratic transport between the exercise's reweighted Gaussian mixtures

The signed mean difference gives a lower bound on every coupling, whereas
one common-noise plan supplies the upper bound. No optimizer is required.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianMixtureWasserstein

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal

/-- Statistical Optimal Transport, Chapter 1, Exercise 6. For the literal
unit-variance mixtures and positive center separation parameter, the
quadratic Wasserstein distance lies between `m / 2` and `m`. -/
theorem wassersteinDistance_gaussianMixtures_bounds (m : ℝ) (hm : 0 < m) :
    let μ := (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) • gaussianReal (-m) 1 + (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) • gaussianReal m 1
    let ν := (1 / 4 : ℝ≥0∞) • gaussianReal (-m) 1 + (3 / 4 : ℝ≥0∞) • gaussianReal m 1
    ENNReal.ofReal (m / 2) ≤ WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ ν ∧
      WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ ν ≤ ENNReal.ofReal m := by
  intro μ ν
  have hhalf : (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) + 1 / 2 = 1 := by
    rw [ENNReal.div_add_div_same, show (1 : ℝ≥0∞) + 1 = 2 by norm_num,
      ENNReal.div_self (by norm_num) (by simp)]
  have hquarter : (1 / 4 : ℝ≥0∞) + 3 / 4 = 1 := by
    rw [ENNReal.div_add_div_same, show (1 : ℝ≥0∞) + 3 = 4 by norm_num,
      ENNReal.div_self (by norm_num) (by simp)]
  have probability (a b : ℝ≥0∞) (hab : a + b = 1) :
      IsProbabilityMeasure (a • gaussianReal (-m) 1 + b • gaussianReal m 1) := by
    refine ⟨?_⟩
    simpa only [Measure.add_apply, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, measure_univ, mul_one] using hab
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := probability _ _ hhalf
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := probability _ _ hquarter
  have hthree : (3 / 4 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ∞ := ENNReal.div_ne_top (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  have g₂ (a : ℝ) : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) (gaussianReal a 1) :=
    (memLp_id_gaussianReal' (μ := a) (v := 1) 2 (by simp)).integrable_sq
  have moment (a b : ℝ≥0∞) (ha : a ≠ ∞) (hb : b ≠ ∞) :
      MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) 2 (a • gaussianReal (-m) 1 + b • gaussianReal m 1) := by
    apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq measurable_id.aestronglyMeasurable).2
    exact ((g₂ (-m)).smul_measure ha).add_measure ((g₂ m).smul_measure hb)
  have g₁ (a : ℝ) : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x) (gaussianReal a 1) :=
    (memLp_id_gaussianReal' (μ := a) (v := 1) 2 (by simp)).integrable (by norm_num)
  have mean (a b : ℝ≥0∞) (ha : a ≠ ∞) (hb : b ≠ ∞) :
      (∫ x : ℝ, x ∂(a • gaussianReal (-m) 1 + b • gaussianReal m 1)) =
        a.toReal * (-m) + b.toReal * m := by
    rw [integral_add_measure ((g₁ (-m)).smul_measure ha) ((g₁ m).smul_measure hb),
      integral_smul_measure, integral_smul_measure, integral_id_gaussianReal,
      integral_id_gaussianReal, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]
  have hμmean : (∫ x : ℝ, x ∂μ) = 0 := by
    dsimp [μ]
    rw [mean _ _ (by simp) (by simp)]
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_one, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat]
    ring
  have hνmean : (∫ x : ℝ, x ∂ν) = m / 2 := by
    dsimp [ν]
    rw [mean _ _ (by simp) hthree]
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_one, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat]
    ring
  constructor
  · have hneg : LipschitzWith 1 (fun x : ℝ => -x) := LipschitzWith.mk_one fun x y => by
      simpa only [Real.dist_eq, neg_sub_neg, abs_sub_comm] using
        (le_refl |x - y|)
    have h := WassersteinLipschitzLower.expectation_sub_le_linearCost_and_le_wassersteinDistance
      μ ν (moment _ _ (by simp) (by simp)) (moment _ _ (by simp) hthree) _ hneg
    have hbound := h.1.trans h.2
    change ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ x : ℝ, -x ∂μ) - (∫ x : ℝ, -x ∂ν)) ≤ _ at hbound
    simpa only [integral_neg (fun x : ℝ => x), hμmean, hνmean, neg_zero, zero_sub,
      neg_neg] using hbound
  · obtain ⟨γ, hγ, hcost⟩ := GaussianMixtureCoupling.exists_gaussian_mixture_coupling_cost m
    have hs : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ ν ^ 2 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (m ^ 2) :=
      (WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance_sq_le_lintegral_of_isCoupling μ ν γ hγ).trans_eq hcost
    apply (ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_iff (z := 2) (by norm_num)).1
    rwa [ENNReal.rpow_two, ENNReal.rpow_two, ← ENNReal.ofReal_pow hm.le]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianMixtureWasserstein

steps.title: Check the two laws and their moments
steps.text: Each component is a probability law of finite second moment. The positive weights in each row sum to one, so both weighted sums are probability laws with finite second moments. In particular their first moments exist.
steps.lean: Mathlib supplies probability for each gaussianReal, membership of the identity in L² and the Gaussian first moments. The proof checks the ENNReal weights and uses finite measure scaling and addition of integrable functions.

steps.title: Bound all couplings with a signed test
steps.text: For any real 1-Lipschitz f, its growth from f(0) and the finite second moments ensure integrability. Pull the two expectations back along the marginals of an arbitrary coupling. Lipschitzness bounds the signed joint integrand by the displacement. Because every coupling has total mass one, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the linear cost by the root quadratic cost. Taking the infima in order gives the two comparisons.

steps.title: Evaluate the right sign of the mean gap
steps.text: The first mixture has mean zero. The second has mean m/2 because three quarters of its mass is on the Gaussian centered at m. Use f(x)=−x, not x, for the displayed orientation of the expectation difference.

steps.lean: integral_add_measure, integral_smul_measure and integral_id_gaussianReal compute both means. The proof verifies the Lipschitz condition for the negative identity, then composes the two existing lower inequalities.

steps.title: Construct one feasible plan for the upper side
steps.text: Let Qₐ,ᵦ be the law of (Z+a,Z+b) with a common standard normal draw Z. The affine maps are Borel and the two marginals are Gₐ and Gᵦ. Keep a quarter at the left center and a half at the right center. Move the remaining quarter from left to right. The first marginal receives two left quarters; the second receives one left quarter and the remaining three quarters at the right. Shared noise cancels, so only the move contributes to the quadratic cost.
steps.lean: The Samplinglib GaussianMixtureCoupling theorem constructs the actual plan and proves the marginal equalities and cost. The assembly consumes the witness, not just an assumed cost bound.

steps.title: Take the quadratic infimum, then undo the square
steps.text: The infimum of quadratic costs is at most the cost of this specific feasible plan. Taking nonnegative square roots gives the desired upper bound for m>0. Together with the lower side this proves the comparison with constants independent of m.
steps.lean: Samplinglib’s squared infimum bridge transfers the witness cost to the distance. Mathlib’s strictly increasing positive power on ENNReal turns the squared comparison into the stated upper bound.
